      "Concept Name": "SPI enable state",
      "Unit": "neorv32_spi",

        "I",
        "A"
      ],

        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],

        "bus_rsp_o.data",

        "Confidentiality": "no",

      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could write a divider or prescaler value that stalls or mis-times SPI transfers.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],

      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_spi",

    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Clock-generation pacing pulses and divider count",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_spi",

    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Transfer-engine sequencing state",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_spi",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The state, bit counter, busy indication, and done pulse only order and time transfer steps, so the sequencing-state rule excludes them at lines 282-325 and 340."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "FIFO buffered transmit data",

      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_spi",
      "Merged Into": "C5",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Serial shift-register copies",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_spi",
      "Merged Into": "C4",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "FIFO occupancy and buffer status",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_spi",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The FIFO flags only buffer, gate, or report movement of data and are not information of their own under the buffer-status rules; they appear at lines 160-163, 208, 231, 236, and 256-259."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus access command",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_spi",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The bus request strobe, direction, and address fields are access-command fields for this unit's registers and FIFOs, not pieces of their own, at lines 137-152, 212, and 246."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus response acknowledge and error",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_spi",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The acknowledge repeats the request strobe and the error is tied to a constant, so the bus-handshake-copy rule excludes them at lines 132-134."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "FIFO depth build-time value",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_spi",

    }
  ],

conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write could disable the SPI block, clear queued data, or prevent further transfers.

conceptual assets.information: The prescaler, divider, and high-speed settings determine when SPI clock-enable pulses are generated and therefore the transfer rate. SPI operation depends on these settings to advance the transceiver.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The timing settings are writable from bus data at lines 143-145, so an unauthorized write can alter the transfer rate. Their conditions control whether spi_clk_en is generated and whether the divider advances at lines 371-377, allowing transfers to be stalled or badly timed.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write a divider or prescaler value that stalls or mis-times SPI transfers.

conceptual assets.information: The chip-select state identifies which SPI slave is active or whether all slaves are deselected. Transfers depend on selecting the intended slave, and the active state is also reported in bus readback.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: A bus write supplies chip-select command data at line 213 and the transceiver stores the selected control at line 290, so it can be changed to select the wrong slave. Clearing the control and driving all chip-select outputs inactive can prevent the intended transfer at lines 332 and 352-354.

conceptual assets.information: Transmit data is the byte supplied by the bus and serialized to the external SPI data output. The SPI transmit function depends on preserving and emitting this byte.
